Show less Read more Like 6 Dislike Reply @Zuringa 5 months ago (edited) I'm 68 years old. Have been fascinated by astronomy from a kid, but what I find now is so many people in my age range are ignorant of how much more we know now, than we did then. Heck, we know of 6,000 more planets now! But I have to mention, one of the most upsetting things was losing Pluto as a planet, but one of the highlights was seeing how beautiful Pluto actually is! Dunno if it's because of its name, or (what was) the mystery of it, but Pluto meant a lot to my generation. As for going to Mars. Not in your lifetime, let alone mine. I know you know that Fraser. Oh, and that was a great interview, thanks. Show less Read more Like Dislike Reply @webjunkienl 5 months ago Show less Read more Like 1 Dislike Reply @georgespalding7640 5 months ago (edited) We may be one of the few species in the Galaxy who have the privilege of being able to leave their world because gravity is weak for us and our technology can overcome it. There may be civilizations out there that are fairly advanced but because of strong gravity and a lack of efficient fuels, they may be confined to their planet waiting until eventually an astronomical event will take them out and they will be helpless sitting ducks when it happens. Kind of sad to think of an intelligent species who could not explore beyond their planet.
